newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar closes up vs mark, down vs yen in thin HK.
newsitem.headline: Dollar closes up vs mark, down vs yen in thin HK.

text.p: The dollar closed firmer against the mark but slightly lower against the yen in thin Hong Kong trade on Thursday in the absence of Tokyo and Singapore traders, who were on holiday.
* Late dollar buying by U.S. funds and profit-taking on the mark/yen in the afternoon powered the dollar/mark to a high of 1.5465 before it dipped slightly at the close, dealers said.
* Selling orders from Singaporeans at slightly above 116 yen capped the dollar's rise and confined it to a range of 115.78-116.10 yen, traders said.
* Volume was low until early European traders crept in, dealers said.

* "The strength of the dollar remained unharmed by the New York fall but a brief correction is seen on the dollar, especially on the dollar/yen which rose sharply near the year end," a U.S. bank dealer said.

* "The dollar will probably ease further next week due to expected adjustments from its year-end rally," a European bank dealer said, adding that sterling crosses were also seen under correction pressure.
* The dollar should find good support at above 115 yen and 1.5280 marks before it headed for a new round of rallies, one dealer said.
